jobs.title: Director - Clinical Transformation (Central Zone)
jobs.description:
Click here to apply as an internal applicant.

Req ID: 229359

Location: Central Zone, Halifax Infirmary Robie Street Entrance - QEII

Department: OPCZ Director Clinical Transformation

Type of Employment: Permanent Hourly FT (100%) x 1

Management/Non Union Position

Posting Closing Date: 7-Dec-26

About The Opportunity

The Clinical Transformation Director – Central Zone, provides leadership and oversight to the development of ongoing clinical operational work plans and implementation related to transformation, organizational design and clinical planning that will allow programs and services within the Central Zone to achieve successful transition in alignment with Nova Scotia Health strategic priorities. This will include the identification of opportunities to improve clinical and operational practice and processes.

The Clinical Transformation Director – Central Zone ensures a disciplined approach to transformational planning, with a cross-organizational breadth among portfolios and departments to ensure, on behalf of the Central Zone VP, that intended organizational integration and transformation is occurring on time and on budget and that project related qualitative and quantitative benefits are realized. This role is responsible for the operations of the clinical transformation reporting to the VP Central Zone Operations, including training and change management strategies to support teams through these changes.

About You

We would love to hear from you if you have the following:

Master’s degree in a health discipline or business administration
Three (3) to five (5) years’ experience at a leadership level involved in planning and implementing a variety of large-scale transformational projects and initiatives, provided across several locations with multiple partners and stakeholders
Experience leading transformation projects which included change management, training and communications plans
Experience engaging, mentoring and empowering teams and stakeholders in a collaborative, participatory manner
Experience developing programs and standards to support the vision, goals and objectives of a healthcare organization.
Superior interpersonal, written and oral communication skills.
Excellent organizational, analytical, problem solving and decision-making skills.
Experience utilizing technology to create efficiencies and streamline tracking, retrieval and distribution of information.
Certification in Project Management preferred

Please ensure your resume is up to date and includes all relevant education, experience, training, and certifications.

Hours

Permanent, full-time position; 75 hourly biweekly

Compensation And Benefits

Pay Scale Type: Management

Band: 07

Hourly Rate: $60.02 - $73.53

Annual Salary: $117,039 - $143,383

Successful candidates may be eligible for a comprehensive benefits package, which includes health, dental, and travel insurance; long-term disability and life insurance coverage; and a defined benefit pension plan. Additional wellness, development and employee support programs may also be available.

What You'll Love About Nova Scotia Health

Nova Scotia Health is more than the province's largest provider of health services; we're a team driven by excellence in health, healing and learning. Across hospitals, health centres and community programs, our people deliver innovative, high-quality care that impacts lives across Nova Scotia and Atlantic Canada.

From vibrant city life to scenic coastal communities, Nova Scotia offers a lifestyle as rewarding as the work itself. At Nova Scotia Health, you'll find meaningful career opportunities, supportive teams and the work-life balance to enjoy everything our beautiful province has to offer. Join us and discover why so many people are choosing to call Nova Scotia home.

Once You've Applied

Thank you for your interest in this position. Only those applicants selected for an interview will be contacted.

Nova Scotia Health is committed to being a workforce that is free of discrimination, values diversity, and is representative, at all job levels, of the people we serve. We encourage all qualified applicants who self-identify as Indigenous, Black/African Nova Scotian, Persons of Colour, Foreign Nationals/Newcomers, Persons with Disabilities, 2SLGBTQIA+ to apply and self-identify.

Not Applicable

Employment type

Full-time

Industries

Hospitals and Health Care

jobs.title: Director of Finance
jobs.description:
Our client, a well-established manufacturing organization, is seeking a strategic and hands-on Director of Finance to lead its Canadian finance function.

Reporting to the senior leadership team, this role will be responsible for driving financial performance, strengthening reporting capabilities, and supporting key business initiatives.

Key responsibilities include:
Leading budgeting, forecasting, and financial planning activities
Overseeing monthly, quarterly, and annual financial reporting
Delivering financial analysis and insights to support strategic decision-making
Managing regional P&L reporting and performance analysis
Developing and monitoring financial and operational KPIs
Overseeing cost accounting and job costing within a manufacturing environment
Supporting government audits, compliance, and internal controls
Evaluating acquisition opportunities and participating in M&A due diligence
Partnering closely with operations and business leaders to drive profitability and growth
Leading finance-related transformation initiatives, including ERP optimization and banking platform implementation

The ideal candidate will bring:
CPA designation
Proven finance leadership experience within a manufacturing environment
Strong expertise in FP&A, financial reporting, and cost accounting
A hands-on approach combined with the ability to influence and support business strategy

This opportunity offers significant exposure to executive leadership, strategic projects, and a growing business environment where finance plays a key role in driving performance.

Show less

Seniority level

Director

Employment type

Full-time

Industries

Staffing and Recruiting

jobs.title: Project Finance Director
jobs.description:
Come Build Your Career at Aecon!

Aecon delivers some of the most complex and impactful infrastructure projects — from transformative transportation networks to critical energy, industrial and nuclear programs. The projects we build connect communities and power future generations. With deep roots in North America and a strong footprint internationally, Aecon brings global expertise and proudly serves public and private sector clients through its Construction and Concessions segment.

Safety Always is not only our #1 core value – it is the standard that anchors our culture. We believe the most ambitious projects deserve the most committed people. At Aecon, you won’t just build your career — you’ll help build what matters to enable future generations to thrive.

At Aecon, You Can Count On

Safety Always. Our number one core value. The safety of our people, projects, partners, and stakeholders is our priority focus – today and always.
Integrity. We lead by example, with humility and courage.
Accountability. We’re passionate about delivering on our commitments.
Inclusion. We provide opportunities where people feel valued, supported, and empowered to contribute fully.

We deliver infrastructure with purpose, and our people are at the heart of everything we do. Aecon employees are incredibly proud to build some of the most impactful infrastructure of this generation – we call it Aecon Proud
.

At Aecon We

Ensure you and your family receive the services and benefits needed to support your mental, emotional, and physical well-being.
Are intentional when it comes to investing in your development. We help you build your career and advance your skills through our Aecon University, tuition reimbursement, and Leadership Programs.
Are committed to creating work environments focused on mutual respect, teamwork, collaboration, and new ideas, through meaningful initiatives, training, partnerships with Veteran groups, our Aecon Women in Trades and diversity programs, as well as our Employee Resource Groups (ERGs), to ensure we are building with top talent and harnessing our collective strengths within every aspect of our culture.
Operate responsibly by managing risk, safety, and environmental considerations across all our projects and surrounding communities.

Our success is built on the passion, expertise, and dedication of our people. Together, we embrace strong execution, innovation, and continuous improvement — values that come to life through the unique talents and collaborative spirit of every team member. If you’re inspired to make a difference through future-building projects, join our best-in-class team.

What is the Opportunity?

Reporting directly to the Director, Finance, the Director, Project Finance will have a comprehensive knowledge of managing large-scale, complex construction projects, Aecon Nuclear administrative operations, mentor staff in the management of accounting practices, complete financial reporting, and oversee all Finance and Accounting processes on site for the Darlington New Nuclear Program (DNNP).

This position will work closely with the DNNP Integrated Project Delivery Project Directors and project teams, as well as the client, OPG.

What You’ll Do Here

Provides financial reporting to meet customer, partner, and site team requirements
Reviews monthly project forecasts, manages the month-end close deliverables for the Aecon-managed General Partnerships, and facilitates month-end and ongoing project reporting as required
Participates in Quarterly forecasts / Annual Business Plans / Budgets
Reviews partner invoices for completion and accurate costing, oversees billings to the client
Helps resolve any disputed billings and takes steps necessary to ensure the timely release of payments from the client
Ensures job costs are monitored and forecasted
Responsible for foreign exchange projection and initiating any hedges or Letters of Credit required in conjunction with the Aecon Treasury team
Participates in the gathering of financial information needed for claims or change order requests
Reviews contracts and changes for commercial terms, including insurance requirements and provides advice on how to mitigate risk in these areas
Supports GP Project management with strategic planning and business case analysis
Delivers monthly project financial updates in leadership forums
Responsible for reviewing cash flow forecasts with site teams and GP partner finance teams
Identifying efficiencies, enhancing processes and working files to provide high-quality, timely information
Overseeing and mentoring Project Finance team and junior staff
Managing relationships with various stakeholders including OPG, Project leadership, GP partners, internal leadership and internal/external auditors

What You Bring to the Team

Strong experience managing the Finance and Accounting aspects of large-scale projects, with a history of cost plus or target price contracts
Advanced working knowledge of an ERP and Excel, with experience with SAP, Business Objects, PowerBI an asset
Completion of a post-secondary degree and Accounting Designation
Minimum of 7 to 10 years of post-qualification related experience, ideally in the construction industry.
Strong knowledge of IFRS, including technical accounting and reporting requirements.
The right individual for this role will have strong leadership skills, be a highly motivated, team-oriented person with strong attention to detail who enjoys building relationships and working with Operations teams towards a common goal.
Strong interpersonal and communication skills (verbal and written) are extremely important in this role.
Able to work on site

Reason for vacancy: New  

Pay range: $150,000 - $170,000. 

Aecon fosters diversity, inclusion and belonging within and across our organization. We welcome all to apply including, women, visible minorities, Indigenous peoples, persons with disabilities, and persons of any sexual orientation or gender identity.

We are committed to adhering to the objectives and requirements outlined in the Accessible Canada Act (ACA), and to meeting the accessibility needs of persons with disabilities in a timely manner. Through the implementation of the requirements of the ACA and its applicable regulations, appropriate accommodations will be provided upon request throughout the interview and hiring process.

As part of our commitment to fair and transparent hiring practices, Aecon may use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to assist in screening and reviewing candidates. These tools are applied responsibly and in accordance with applicable privacy laws and Aecon’s AI Usage Policy. All final decisions are made by qualified Aecon team members.

Show more

Seniority level

Not Applicable

Employment type

Full-time

Industries

Construction
